context: Cover skin and avoid standing water when you can, so fewer mosquitoes bite. A plant on the skin does not replace that, and it does not treat diseases mosquitoes can carry.

Camp site: pick flat ground out of a drainage, off the ridge, and clear of dead limbs. Face the opening away from the night wind. A spot near a stream is handy and also a flood risk, so step uphill a little. This is planning, not a permit to camp where rules forbid it.

Sleep: insulation under you matters as much as the cover over you. Change out of wet clothes before you lie down, and keep a dry layer in the bag. Food and scented items stay outside the sleep spot. A closed shelter still needs air. This note does not treat cold injury.

Kitchen: cook and store food downwind of where you sleep, and seal it so animals are not fed. Drown the fire or stove and feel for heat before you leave. Strain cloudy water, then boil it, before it goes in the pot. Known food only. This is not a foraging menu.

Sanitation: carry waste out when the land requires it. Otherwise dig a small cathole well away from water, camp, and trails, then cover it. Soap stays out of the creek. Hands are cleaned away from the stream. This is a hygiene reminder, not a medical treatment.

Leave the site: pack out what you carried in, put back natural cover you moved, and drown the fire until it is cold. The next person should not be able to tell you cooked there. A waypoint you saved stays on your device. Erasing the camp from the land is the point.
